theorems.name: Existence of Power Series Solutions
theorems.statement: If x0 is an ordinary point, y''+p(x)y'+q(x)y=0 has two linearly independent power series solutions about x0, converging at least out to the nearest singular point (real or complex).
theorems.conditions: p, q must be analytic at x0.
theorems.intuition: Substituting a power series and matching coefficients always succeeds at an ordinary point.
theorems.proofSketch: Standard existence theory for analytic ODEs; the recurrence relation determines all coefficients from a0,a1.
theorems.example: The Airy equation y''-xy=0 has two independent series solutions about x=0.
theorems.examReady: Identify ordinary point, substitute series, re-index, extract recurrence.

theorems.name: Laplace Transform of Derivatives
theorems.conditions: f must be of exponential order for the transform to exist.
theorems.intuition: Integration by parts converts each derivative into multiplication by s, minus an initial-condition correction.
theorems.proofSketch: Integrate by parts once for f', apply twice for f''.
theorems.example: Solving y''-3y'+2y=0, y(0)=1, y'(0)=0 via transform + partial fractions.
theorems.examReady: Transform both sides, solve algebraically for Y(s), invert via partial fractions.
